diagnosis: The model frequently fails to predict off-topic shifts, often generating detailed continuations of the dominant narrative when the true news is unrelated. When topic does continue, the model over-predicts constructive dialogue and de-escalation even when historical news shows clear escalation or confrontational signals, leading to tone mismatches. The model also invents specific diplomatic events (e.g., meetings, statements) not supported by the history.
suggestions: When historical news shows escalating conflict, canceled visits, or sharp criticism, do not automatically predict de-escalation or constructive talks; instead, reflect the likely continuation or intensification of the confrontational tone.

Explicitly consider that the next article may be off-topic entirely, especially when the historical news compresses many entries on a single narrow event; assign higher probability to a shift in subject matter rather than assuming a linear narrative continuation.

Do not invent specific meetings, statements, or diplomatic steps unless the historical news provides strong and direct evidence that such events are scheduled or have occurred; prefer generic descriptions of the situation when details are absent.
